findings.claim: For any focused regression-selection decision, record the concrete test/configuration and consumer identity, and check selection quality against the broader suite before treating reduced execution as adequate.

research.source: Bavishi et al., “An empirical comparison of four Java-based regression test selection techniques,” Journal of Systems and Software 186 (2022), article 111174, DOI 10.1016/j.jss.2021.111174; published publisher abstract/index.
research.status: Search-indexed publisher abstract; direct open returned HTTP 403, so full paper was not inspected.
research.support: Study compares four RTS techniques on revisions from five open-source Java projects; reports differing safety/precision, and selected suites had 8.75% lower fault-detection ability than the original suite. Selection can save time but can lose detection ability.
research.applicability: Supports checking selection safety/precision and retaining a broader/full-suite qualification boundary. Does not quantify risk for this C++/Rust/CMake/GUI repository or for hand-picked targeted tests.

findings.decision_use: Reject making diff-to-test selection the only acceptance evidence for any of R01-R08. Use changed helper/caller and selected configuration to choose a focused diagnostic; retain the exact broader acceptance requirement and report what selection cannot cover.
predicted_alternatives: If symptom follows a particular configured consumer/provider or selected retained input, target that path and configuration.
If symptom reproduces across the relevant configured consumers, suspect shared helper/state or a broader contract and widen coverage.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: For a chosen report, preserve commit, exact configuration/cache, executable/provider/input identity and matched input; run one focused existing fixture or tiny offline fixture through the actual helper-to-consumer path, comparing the relevant configurations. Only widen after the focused check discriminates or leaves a coverage gap.
findings.limits: No configuration or consumer for the hypothetical reports is known; no tests were run. A selection result is not fault-detection proof.

findings.claim: Configuration-aware selection is valuable where the software actually has modeled product variants, but evidence for SPL-wide sampling does not establish coverage for this repository’s ordinary build options or providers.

research.source: Jung, Kang, Lee, “Automated code-based test selection for software product line regression testing,” Journal of Systems and Software 158 (2019), article 110419, DOI 10.1016/j.jss.2019.110419; published publisher abstract/index.
research.status: Search-indexed publisher abstract and indexed excerpts; direct open returned HTTP 403, so full paper was not inspected.
research.support: Evaluated on six product lines; reports average end-to-end regression-time reduction of 14.8–49.1% against repeatedly applying a single-product RTS technique. The paper conditions its no-missed-fault claim on Rothermel assumptions and deterministic product-line runs.
research.applicability: Useful only by analogy when valid configurations/feature variability are explicit and selection has configuration-to-code/test mappings. No such feature model or SPL claim is supplied here.

findings.decision_use: For R03 provider, R04/R05/R06 adapter/host, and R07/R08 feature/build variants, require exact selected options/provider/host and test-registration gates before reusing another configuration’s result. Do not prescribe exhaustive combination testing or assume the SPL result transfers.
predicted_alternatives: If test registration/consumer path changes with the configuration, one configuration’s pass does not cover another.
If the relevant path and inputs are shared and configuration-independent, a focused common-path test may discriminate without a configuration matrix.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: Capture the active CMake cache/options, provider/package identity, selected executable or adapter, and registered case; compare only the two implicated configurations with the same inputs and consumer assertion.
findings.limits: Only six SPLs and stated determinism/safety assumptions; search snippet does not expose full threat analysis. Actual project configuration and gates are unknown.

findings.claim: Environment/setup differences can confound repeated-failure interpretation; preserve environment identity and classify setup failure separately, but do not presume resource pressure causes flakiness.

research.source: Berndt, Bach, Baltes, “Do Test and Environmental Complexity Increase Flakiness? An Empirical Study of SAP HANA,” ESEM ’24, DOI 10.1145/3674805.3695407; published ACM/IEEE conference paper, full author-hosted paper opened.
research.status: Full 10-page paper inspected. Primary single-industry study; authors explicitly caution about SAP HANA external validity and confounding (paper lines 691-705).
research.support: Two 12-week SAP HANA datasets (production and targeted experiments; >1.5M test results) found execution-time/flakiness correlations (r=.74 and .79), but no significant relationship with system load; CPU/memory relationship was inconclusive (lines 24-44, 662-706, 714-738). Authors caution splitting tests adds setup overhead (lines 611-619).
research.applicability: Supports logging matched setup/environment and separating setup failures from product failures. Does not establish that the assumed 8 CPU/16 GiB campaign envelope is adequate, that capacity explains a report, or that an un-repeated failure is flaky.

findings.decision_use: A missing dependency, wrong provider/build option, unavailable test host/display, or invalid build tree is a setup outcome. A valid setup that fails on matched inputs is product evidence. Keep BUILD_JOBS, CMAKE_BUILD_PARALLEL_LEVEL, effective worker budget, host/platform, provider, and relevant cache/input identity with any result.
predicted_alternatives: Failure only under a distinct setup/configuration suggests environment or consumer-selection confounding.
Failure repeats with identical setup and input through the same consumer strengthens a product-path hypothesis.
Inconsistent repetitions remain unresolved/flaky until enough controlled evidence distinguishes product nondeterminism from environment effects.
findings.cheapest_discriminator: Before execution, validate the exact prerequisite/configuration with a minimal offline/helper fixture; then repeat only the focused check with identical source, input, options, and environment identity. Do not launch broad builds to diagnose a helper.
